opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
“The LORD is near to all who call upon him,
to all who call upon him in truth.” — Psalm 145:18

I’m going to be honest.  I’ve been delayed in writing these reflections. I missed Mass this past Sunday. I can’t believe we’re already in the fourth week of Lent.
And it brings up a real question: do I even feel worthy of God?  A God who suffered for our redemption.
A God who sees our fallenness clearly—and still wants us. Because that’s not how human relationships usually work.

Most relationships have conditions. Some are subtle, some are obvious. Expectations, disappointments, unspoken limits. Even love can feel like it depends on performance, consistency, or being “good enough.”

But God is not like that.

The Psalm says He is near to all who call upon Him—in truth. Not perfection. Not performance. Truth.  And the truth is, sometimes things feel messy.

The ground feels muddy.
The mind feels tangled.
Old hurts resurface and take hold.
Greed creeps in.
Love falters.

We know this about ourselves and Christ knows it too.

He entered into our humanity fully. Not from a distance, but from within it. He knew the pull of human weakness, the weight of suffering, the reality of temptation. And yet He remained rooted in the Father—living out what He was sent to do, guided by One who sees clearly and completely.  That matters.  Because it means nothing you are experiencing right now is hidden from Him. Nothing disqualifies you from turning back.

Lent, then, is not a measure of how well you’ve performed. It’s not a checklist you either passed or failed.

It’s an invitation.

Even now—halfway through, imperfect, delayed, distracted—the invitation is still open.  Not to escape difficulty, but to face it differently. To embrace the crosses you carry, not by force, but by asking:

What is this teaching me?
What needs to change in me?
Where am I being refined?

And maybe most importantly: Can I bring this to God honestly? Because that is what He responds to.

Not appearances.
Not a polished effort.
Truth.

The Psalm does not say the Lord is near to those who have everything together.  It says He is near to those who call upon Him in truth.

So call.

Even now.

Especially now.
